text:
Nina (eng): Quick follow-up from todays all-hands re: KMS/BYOQ + audit exports. Im collecting a short FAQ for customers asking about ISO/SOC evidence. Main asks: can we prove key provenance? how long can customers keep logs? how does Private affect auditability?

Jordan (security): Good questions. Short version: key provenance = we emit signing attestations for service-managed keys; for BYOQ we store an HSM attestation blob (not the key). Well provide a downloadable materials package for audits (manifest + signed checksum).

Tara (compliance): For ISO/SOC2 auditors they usually want: 1) rotation history, 2) access control change logs, 3) integrity proof for exported logs. We can produce a .tar.gz with a manifest.json that lists objects + SHA256, plus a signed envelope from our signing key. That addresses integrity requirements.

Nina (eng): Nice. What about retention? We heard 90d default in hosted. Are there hard limits?

Ibrahim (infra): Hosted default = 90d. Customers can request archive exports to their bucket for any retention period. We recommend lifecycle rules like this example to move to Glacier after 60d:
```xml
<LifecycleConfiguration>
  <Rule>
    <ID>audit-archive</ID>
    <Status>Enabled</Status>
    <Filter><Prefix>exports/</Prefix></Filter>
    <Transition>
      <Days>60</Days>
      <StorageClass>GLACIER</StorageClass>
    </Transition>
  </Rule>
</LifecycleConfiguration>
```

Sam (sales): Is there a simple line we can give customers: "How long will Redwood keep my audit logs?"

Tara (compliance): Suggested customer-facing phrasing: "Default retention is 90 days. Customers may configure daily export to a customer-owned storage for longer retention and compliance needs; Redwood can provide signed export bundles for audit evidence."

Nina (eng): About Private/VPC: does control-plane proxying remove auditability? Any gaps?

Jordan (security): No gaps. Control-plane events are still logged at the edge and included in exports. For Private with customer-managed networking we also include vpc/policy identifiers in records. Note: data-plane inference payloads are not stored unless customer enable full-log export.

Ibrahim (infra): Small ops note: full-log export has storage and egress costs; we surface estimated monthly cost in the console when you enable it. Also, we truncate captured payloads at 10k bytes by default (configurable per-customer with opt-in).

Nina (eng): Any example of the export filename/structure so customers can show auditors?

Jordan (security): Example structure: exports/YYYY-MM-DD/{tenant-id}/audit-blob-YYYYMMDDT000000.tar.gz. Inside: manifest.json, events.ndjson.gz, signatures.asc. manifest.json contains object list + checksums.

Ops Bot: Note: Security office hours "Audit exports deep dive" on 1971208800. RSVP: https://calendar.redwood.company/officehours-security.

Sam (sales): Thanks  can you drop that one-liner + example structure in the shared sales enablement doc? Ill push to customers.

Tara (compliance): Action items: Jordan to prepare the audit bundle template by EOW, Ibrahim to add retention/lifecycle example to docs, Nina to add FAQ to customer-facing page.

Nina (eng): Awesome  Ill assemble the FAQ and ping legal for wording on BYOQ attestation. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
